definitions.explanation: Grapes that have been dried, either in the sun or by other methods. A common snack and baking ingredient in Japan.

examples.japanese: {干|ほ}しぶどう{入|い}り⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦パン→パン：00553_pan⟧。
⟦サラダ→サラダ：01364_sarada⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{干|ほ}しぶどう⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{加|くわ}えた→加える：01941_kuwaeru⟧。
examples.english: I added raisins to the salad.

examples.japanese: {干|ほ}しぶどう⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{鉄分|てつぶん}→鉄分：19444_tetsubun⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{豊富|ほうふ}→豊富：03620_houfu⟧で、⟦おやつ→おやつ：17921_oyatsu⟧⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{人気|にんき}→人気：01488_ninki⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: Raisins are rich in iron and popular as a snack.

notes:
Composed of {干|ほ}し (dried — from ⟦{干|ほ}す→干す：00115_hosu⟧, to dry) + ぶどう ({葡萄|ぶどう}, grapes). A straightforward compound following the common Japanese pattern of {干|ほ}し + food name for dried foods.

USAGE:
The English loanword ⟦レーズン→レーズン：12843_reezun⟧ is also very common in Japan and may be more frequently used in commercial and culinary contexts (especially baking). {干|ほ}しぶどう is the native Japanese term and is understood by everyone.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {干|ほ}しぶどう{入|い}り — containing raisins
- {干|ほ}しぶどう⟦パン→パン：00553_pan⟧ — raisin bread
- {干|ほ}しぶどう⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{入|い}れる→入れる：01098_ireru⟧ — to add raisins

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦レーズン→レーズン：12843_reezun⟧ — raisin (English loanword; common in recipes and product names)
- ぶどう — grape (fresh, not dried)
- ⟦{干|ほ}し{柿|がき}→干し柿：28314_hoshigaki⟧ — dried persimmon (another traditional Japanese dried fruit)
